issues.what: Cliopatria's oversize Panthay shape (Kunming, east Yunnan, Sichuan basin, Guizhou/Chongqing edges, about 1,300 cells) is cut from the Panthay state but left out of the Qing keyframes too, so it is nobody's from 1856; the Qing 1859 shape also drops Sichuan/Chongqing (272 cells) and the 30 Jiujiang cells. The page puts the rebels at Dali and calls Sichuan a province 'not in rebellion'.

Wuchang retaken by Qing forces in December 1856: the Taiping 1856 keyframe keeps it all year and the 1857 snap sends the 216 cells of the Wuhan area to nobody (grey hole in the Taiping block 1857-1859, Qing never gets it).
issues.patch: keyframe_overrides/3 (Taiping 1856 without Wuhan 120 km) and /0-2 (Qing hold Wuhan)

issues.what: Aigun contest: the gazetteer's Outer Manchuria takes in all of Khabarovsk krai, so 1,708 cells of Okhotsk-coast land that Russia held before 1858 and the Qing never held were drawn contested with the Qing. The contest is now limited to the Amur's left bank and Primorye inside the Qing's own 1857 shape (3,919 cells); that the Qing refused to ratify and the Ussuri condominium stay as drawn.

Brazil / New Granada size-rule conflict of 766 cells in 1853: the smaller New Granada won, then its keyframe sent the 741 cells of the upper Rio Negro (Amazonas, Brazil) to nobody, a grey hole in every year from 1853 although both dossiers' 1853 shapes and Cliopatria give them to Brazil.

Same land in 1850-1852: New Granada holds 850 cells of the upper Rio Negro and Japurá including São Gabriel da Cachoeira (its 1834 keyframe, 'smaller portions of ... Brazil'), while the Amazonas page has the comarca of Rio Negro in the Empire from 1824, a fort at São Gabriel from 1761, and the frontier with Colombia undefined until the 1908 treaty. The page does not say who held it in 1850-52 and Brazil's own dossier holds it only as a 1853 claim, so it is left.

The umbrella british-colonial-empire row took 2,444 cells of New South Wales (and Queensland) from the colony in 1856 and the colony took them back in 1859 (2,692-cell snap); no event or page supports a transfer (Queensland separated from New South Wales in 1859). The BCE overrides drop the colony land but keep the 407 coastal cells the row already held in 1853-55.

About 410 cells of British India (Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand) outside the Raj's 1858 outline were nobody's at the end of 1858 only (the British Empire row's dissolve of 1 Nov sweeps them to nobody; the 1859 keyframe snap hands them to the Raj). The Raj 1858 keyframe now uses its 1859 outline.

Egypt (muhammad-ali-dynasty) is direct from Nov 1840: ottoman-empire/ledger/186 is a Levant-only vassal_end but the compile closes the whole Ottoman-Egypt vassal relation. The 1841 firmans 'emphasiz[e] his position as vassal'; the dossier itself says vassal throughout to 1865. Reopened for 1850-1859 (runs to the dossier's own 1865 end).

Size-rule conflicts where the smaller, separate state rightly won: Nian rebels over Taiping in Anhui/Henan (764), Chan Santa Cruz over Mexico (402), Manipur, Bhutan (Duars), Nepal, Kolhapur, Jhalawar, Bundi, Bharatpur, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Bhopal over the Company/British Empire (until 1858), Swazi over the South African Republic, Herat over Qajar Persia (1856-59, Persian capture contest of 1856 is drawn), Kengtung over Qing, Bosnia eyalet over Austria, Satsuma over the shogunate, Mexico over the USA on a few border-edge cells (Arizona 29, Texas 24, New Mexico 4 cell-years; the Gadsden Purchase of 1854 is in the dossiers' ledgers).
Lunda keyframe of 1856 is a large disc: it takes 144 cells of Kuba (leaving Kuba an arc) and 112 of Luba, and loses 272 cells to nobody. Cliopatria-driven; I did not open a page on it.

Unresolved places: british-gold-coast ledger/1 and keyframe 1850 ('Keta', Ghana) and akyem-abuakwa ledger/2 ('Akwamufie'): the gazetteer lacks both names. The Danish forts' cells (3) go to the british-colonial-empire row, same colour; the Akwamufie loss is a few cells. Not worth a replacement region.

Skipped events: german-confederation umbrella losses/contest_end 1850-52 (no cells) and colony-of-tasmania ledger/3 1856 (no land) need nothing. Russia's 1859 snap (328 cells) only fills lakes (Baikal, Ladoga) that Cliopatria also shows as nobody; the NE British Columbia wedge and the Oman interior (Dhofar, Al Wusta nobody after 1856) match Cliopatria.
